description:
The only surah beginning with the discrete Arabic letters Alif Lām Mīm that also contains a ayah which requires one who recites it to perform a **Prostration** of bowing down to the ground before God in worship at the mention of God's revealed signs. It takes its name from verse 15 which mentions "prostration" (sajdah). The surah emphasized the truth of the Quran at the beginning, and the Prophet is urged at the end of the surah to pay no attention to the disbelievers who cannot see the significance of God's signs.
The surah is also known as: Bowing Down, Bowing down in Worship, The Adoration, Worship.

4.1: That is, in six periods of time. Cf. <{["Q", "57:4"]}>.

5.2: That is, in a period of time.

10.1: That is, 'Shall we be brought forth again after our bodies have decomposed and all traces of our physical remains have disappeared in the ground?'

16.1: That is, they abandon their beds at night and forgo the pleasure of sleep to worship their Lord in a state of fear and hope.

21.1: Or 'this side of the greater punishment,' or 'aside from the greater punishment.'
21.2: By 'the nearer punishment' is meant the afflictions and hardships the faithless may be made to suffer in the world with the purpose of bringing them back to Allah and in order to save them from the greater punishment of the Hereafter.

translations.2: The [gradual] sending down of the Book, there is no doubt in it, is from the Lord of all the worlds.
translations.3: Do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? Rather it is the truth from _your_ Lord, that _you_ may warn a people to whom there did not come any warner before _you_, so that they may be guided [to the right path].
translations.4: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days,<{["F", 1]}> then He settled on the Throne. You do not have besides Him any guardian or intercessor. Will you not then take admonition?
translations.5: He directs the command<{["F", 1]}> from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends toward Him in a day<{["F", 2]}> whose span is a thousand years by your reckoning.
translations.6: That is the Knower of the sensible and the Unseen, the All-mighty, the All-merciful,
translations.7: who perfected everything that He created, and commenced man's creation from clay.
translations.8: Then He made his progeny from an extract of a base fluid.
translations.9: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit, and made for you the hearing, the sight, and the hearts. Little do you thank.
translations.10: They say, 'When we have been lost in the dust,<{["F", 1]}> shall we be indeed created anew?' Rather they disbelieve in the encounter with their Lord.
translations.11: _Say_, 'You will be taken away by the angel of death, who has been charged with you. Then you will be brought back to your Lord.'
translations.12: Were _you_ to see when the guilty hang their heads before their Lord [confessing], 'Our Lord! We have seen and heard. Send us back so that we may act righteously. Indeed we are [now] convinced.'
translations.13: Had We wished We would have given every soul its guidance, but My word became due [against the defiant]: 'Surely I will fill hell with all the [guilty] jinn and humans.'<{["F", 1]}>
translations.14: So taste [the punishment] for your having forgotten the encounter of this day of yours. We [too] have forgotten you. Taste the everlasting punishment because of what you used to do.
translations.15: Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and celebrate the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
translations.16: Their sides vacate their beds<{["F", 1]}> to supplicate their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have provided them.
translations.17: No one knows what has been kept hidden for them of comfort as a reward for what they used to do.
translations.18: Is someone who is faithful like someone who is a transgressor? They are not equal.
translations.19: As for those who have faith and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens of the Abode —a hospitality for what they used to do.
translations.20: As for those who have transgressed, their refuge is the Fire. Whenever they seek to leave it, they will be turned back into it, and they will be told: 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.'
translations.21: We shall surely make them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment,<{["F", 1]}> so that they may come back.<{["F", 2]}>
translations.22: Who is a greater wrongdoer than him who is reminded of his Lord's signs, whereat he disregards them? Indeed We shall take vengeance upon the guilty.
translations.23: Certainly We gave Moses the Book, [declaring], 'Do not be in doubt about the encounter with Him,' and We made it a [source of] guidance for the Children of Israel.
translations.24: And amongst them We appointed _imam_s to guide [the people] by Our command, when they had been patient and had conviction in Our signs.
translations.25: Indeed _your_ Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ.
translations.26: Does it not dawn upon them how many generations We have destroyed before them, amid [the ruins of] whose dwellings they walk? There are indeed signs in that. Will they not then listen?
translations.27: Do they not see that We carry water to the parched earth and with it We bring forth crops of which they eat, themselves and their cattle? Will they not then see?
translations.28: And they say, 'When will this judgement be, should you be truthful?'
translations.29: _Say_, 'On the day of judgement their [newly found] faith shall not avail the faithless, nor will they be granted any respite.'
translations.30: So _turn away_ from them, and _wait_. They too are waiting.
